name: Ring Push-Up with Feet on Swiss Ball
description: An extreme instability push-up variation combining gymnastic rings for the hands and a swiss ball for the feet. Both surfaces are unstable, requiring the entire kinetic chain — from wrist through shoulder, core, hip, and ankle — to continuously stabilize while executing the pressing movement. This creates maximal demand on stabilizer muscles across the full body while still loading the pectoralis major through the pressing range.

execution.starting_position: Set rings low (push-up position height). Place a swiss ball behind the rings. Get into push-up position with hands in the rings and feet resting on the swiss ball. Establish full-body stability before the first rep.
execution.setup_instructions: Set rings at appropriate height for push-ups. Fully inflate the ball. Position ball directly behind rings. Getting into position requires care — have a training partner assist initially.
steps: Step 1: Establish a controlled plank with hands in rings and feet on swiss ball. Take several breaths to find balance.
Step 2: Slowly lower the chest toward the ring level, managing ring rotation and ball roll simultaneously.
Step 3: Descend until chest is at ring level — this is a very challenging position to maintain.
Step 4: Press back to the starting position with full control. Reset between each rep if needed.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale before descent, exhale on press. Breathing is controlled and deliberate.
common_mistakes: Attempting without mastering ring push-ups and elevated-feet push-ups separately first
Moving too fast — this exercise requires slow, deliberate movement
Ball positioned too far back — it should be close enough that feet don't have to reach
safety_considerations: Have a training partner present for safety on the first several attempts
Have a clear plan to safely exit the position if stability is lost
Prerequisites: solid ring push-ups AND swiss ball feet-elevated push-ups
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range is the goal, but partial range with full control is acceptable while mastering the exercise.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the rings and the ball simultaneously — pressure in both directions creates stability
Every rep is a new challenge — reset mentally before each descent
